clue.text: Woman prepared to rise, supporting popular uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so the earlier piece goes on top

parts.note: something popular is in, in fashion

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the words woman and prepared are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
fit, as in fit for the task, means prepared

explanation.surface: A woman gets ready to rise up in support of a popular revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to rise' reads the woman and 'prepared' upwards, and 'supporting' puts that below the word for popular.
explanation.definitionFit: The intifada is the Palestinian popular uprising; the Arabic word means a shaking off.

clue.text: Pothead to be sick in bucket

parts.note: the head of the word pot is its first letter, P
to ail is to be ill or sick

explanation.surface: A cannabis smoker throws up into a bucket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pothead' is read as the head of 'pot', its first letter, not a drug user.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is a bucket, a straight synonym for an open vessel with a handle.

clue.text: Climbing plant, climbing, snags good strip of skin

indicators.note: snags means catches and holds, so one piece takes the other inside it
in a down clue climbing means the word for the plant is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a liana is a tropical climbing vine

explanation.surface: A climbing vine catches a strip of skin as someone climbs past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns LIANA into ANAIL, which then 'snags' G between its A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnail is a hangnail, a torn strip of skin beside a fingernail.

clue.text: Name-dropping spinster resolved to keep going

indicators.note: resolved means sorted out or broken down, so the remaining letters are rearranged
name-dropping is read as dropping N, the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A determined unmarried woman who drops names is set on carrying on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name-dropping' takes N out of SPINSTER, leaving SPISTER, and 'resolved' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to carry on steadily despite obstacles, to continue without stopping.

clue.text: Want coast to receive label

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the label goes inside the coast word

parts.note: the shore is the coast
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: Someone wants the coastline to be given an official label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' looks like a verb here but is the noun meaning lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Want as a noun means lack or deficiency, the state of having too little of something.

clue.text: Hymn to periodical pong curtailed by one sort of scanner

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: niff is British slang for a bad smell, a pong
one is the Roman numeral I
a CAT scanner is a medical body scanner

explanation.surface: An oddly specific hymn praising a magazine, a bad smell and a hospital scanner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' trims NIFF (British slang for a stink) to NIF.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magnificat is the canticle of the Virgin Mary, a hymn sung at evensong and vespers.

clue.text: Pressure garment protecting centre of wound

indicators.note: protecting means covering round, so the garment goes round the other piece

parts.note: a dress is a garment

indicators.note: centre of means the middle letter of the word wound

explanation.surface: A pressure garment is wrapped round the middle of a wound as a dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' picks U, the middle of WOUND, and 'protecting' wraps DRESS round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is coercion, pressure or threats used to force someone to act.

clue.text: Symbol not beginning to draw into web

indicators.note: not beginning means losing the first letter

parts.note: a pentangle is a five-pointed star used as a symbol

explanation.surface: A symbol that isn't the starting point for drawing a spider's web.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not beginning' strips the P from PENTANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to catch and trap something in a mesh or snare.

clue.text: Break South American state holding one back

indicators.note: back means the whole assembled string is read in reverse
holding means containing, so the state takes the other piece inside

parts.note: Utah is a US state
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A break for a South American country holding someone back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American state' looks like one unit; it is S plus Utah. UTAH 'holding' I gives UTAIH; S + UTAIH read 'back' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a pause or gap in continuity, an interruption.

clue.text: Cultivate cash carrier

definitions.meaning: to ... the soil is to plough and cultivate it
a shop's cash drawer or register holds the money taken

explanation.surface: Grow crops and carry the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: tilling land is cultivating it, and a shop's till is the drawer holding the cash.

clue.text: Bird keeper's cartel breaking wind

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so the cartel word goes inside the wind word

parts.note: Auster is the south wind, from Latin
a ring is a cartel, a group of dealers acting together

explanation.surface: A falconer's syndicate breaks wind.
explanation.walkthrough: AUSTER is the classical name for the south wind.
explanation.definitionFit: An austringer is a falconer who keeps and flies goshawks and other short-winged hawks.

clue.text: Jump back, receiving Catholic item in post

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the reversed word holds the other piece
back means the jump word is read in reverse

parts.note: to leap is to jump
RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Someone recoils on getting a Catholic item through the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LEAP into PAEL, which 'receiving' RC becomes PA-RC-EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is a wrapped package sent by mail, an item in the post.

clue.text: Swapped baby cherub in divinatory system — one's gone missing

indicators.note: in means the cherub word is placed inside the other
gone missing means the one, I, is removed

parts.note: the I Ching is the Chinese system of divination by hexagrams
one is the Roman numeral I
a cherub is an angel

explanation.surface: A baby swapped at birth, with a cherub in an occult system and somebody missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The I Ching is a Chinese book of divination; 'gone missing' drops I (one) to leave CHING, and ANGEL goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a changeling is a fairy child secretly left in place of a stolen human infant.

clue.text: Supposing Romeo's turned in hidden treasure to sea dweller

indicators.note: in means placed inside the hidden treasure word

parts.note: a stash is a hidden hoard

indicators.note: turned means the words for supposing and Romeo are read backwards

parts.note: if means supposing
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: If Romeo turned to buried treasure, he'd end up living under the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes RFI from IF + R, and 'in' puts it in STASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A starfish is a star-shaped echinoderm that lives on the seabed.

clue.text: Tom, perhaps, keeping sloths in discomfort

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the sloths go into the male word

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, an example of a male
an ai is a three-toed sloth, so ais are sloths

explanation.surface: A tomcat ill at ease from having sloths in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The ai is a three-toed sloth, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a general feeling of unease, illness or discomfort.

clue.text: Second deterrent, allegedly loud

parts.note: Trident is Britain's nuclear missile system, claimed to act as a deterrent

explanation.surface: A second deterrent is said to be noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: Trident is the UK's submarine-launched nuclear weapon; 'allegedly' questions whether it really deters, rather than signalling a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud and harsh, grating on the ear.

clue.text: Slightly drunk, admitting copper's an element

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the copper goes inside the drunk word

parts.note: merry means tipsy, slightly drunk
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Tipsy, a policeman claims to be in his element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper's' tempts as a policeman; it is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is a chemical element, the metal that is liquid at room temperature.

clue.text: Ten Arabs affected by pesticide

indicators.note: affected means altered or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten Arabs harmed by a pest-control chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratsbane is rat poison, traditionally arsenic, a substance for killing vermin.

clue.text: Tightwad's self-esteem Tolkienian baddies lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the words are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ego is one's sense of self-esteem
orcs are the brutish villains of Tolkien's Middle-earth

explanation.surface: A miser's pride is stolen by Tolkien's villains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' looks like stolen; in a down clue it reverses EGO + ORCS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge of Dickens's A Christmas Carol is the byword for a miser.

clue.text: Involving transmutation of racy pigs?

indicators.note: transmutation means changing one form into another, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An alchemical process turning lusty swine into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines an alchemical term while also signalling the rearrangement of RACY PIGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spagyric means alchemical, relating to the alchemists' art of changing base metal into gold.

clue.text: More than one friend securing draw, mostly

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the friend word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a lure is a draw or attraction

explanation.surface: A friend securing a mostly drawn game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LURE to LUR, which PAL is 'securing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural is the grammatical number for more than one item.

clue.text: Root around books on summit

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible
atop means on the summit of

explanation.surface: Someone digs about among books on a mountaintop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root around' reads as one phrase, but 'Root' alone is the definition and 'around' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is a root vegetable, strictly a tuber growing underground.

clue.text: Dog keeps family from throwing up

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the family word goes into the dog

parts.note: a pug is a breed of small dog
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A dog stops its family from vomiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Puking is slang for vomiting, bringing food back up.

clue.text: Trendy grub was first to be garnished with mash (or kale, initially)

indicators.note: garnished with means surrounded by a dressing, so the mash goes round the other piece

parts.note: pulp is a mash, a soft squashed mass
to have led is to have been first

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of kale

explanation.surface: A fashionable dish was the first to be served with mash or kale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garnished with' means surrounded by, so the mash word wraps round 'was first'; the bracketed words are part of the wordplay, not an aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulled pork, slow-cooked shredded pork, became a fashionable dish in hip eateries.

clue.text: New recruit to a country

parts.note: a cub is a novice, a new recruit, as in a cub reporter

explanation.surface: A novice joins a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is a Caribbean island nation.

clue.text: Bit of hair left to hound

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog, a hound

explanation.surface: A tuft of fur left on a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A curl is a ringlet or lock, a coiled piece of hair.

clue.text: Something in wine bar turning brown outside

indicators.note: outside means the brown word goes round the other piece

parts.note: tan is a light brown

indicators.note: turning means the bar word is read backwards

parts.note: an inn is a pub, a bar

explanation.surface: A wine bar going brown on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes NNI from INN, and TAN goes 'outside' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tannin is the astringent compound from grape skins and oak that gives red wine its dryness.

clue.text: Endless vigour on horseback causing decay

indicators.note: back means everything is read in reverse
endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: energy is vigour
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Unending energy on horseback leads to rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims ENERGY to ENERG; with NAG it is read 'back', the indicator tucked into 'horseback'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangrene is the death and decay of body tissue.
